newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soy gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soy gains.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly higher on Tuesday, boosted by a late technical rally in soybeans, traders said.
Commodity funds were aggressive sellers of at least 2,000 lots of soymeal in early trade but switched to the buy side late as losses in soybeans triggered technical buy signals.
"Last week's low in the May beans was $8.16 (per bushel)," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "We took that out and then Rosenthal Collins and Cargill started buying."
Traders noted commercial buying interest. Some speculated it was linked to scheduled down time at several plants.

Cargill Inc reportedly bought 500 lots May soymeal and 900 lots May soyoil. The action came after Cargill said two more of its plants in Kansas City and Norfolk, Va., will temporarily close this summer. Cargill earlier said its plant in Guntersville, Ala., was shut due to flooding along the Ohio River, making soybean purchases difficult.
Soymeal closed $1.60 per ton higher to $0.50 lower while soyoil ended 0.24 cent per lb higher to 0.02 lower.
"We had too big of a break in this market in the last few days," said Jason Roose of U.S. Commodities.
"From the demand standpoint, we're still showing that we have tight stocks and you're going to see end-user coverage on any break like this," Roose said.

New crop months were supported by predictions for heavy flooding across much of the central U.S., floor sources said. A National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration report predicted the most widespread spring flooding in a decade.
On the day, SAK Futures sold 1,200 lots May soymeal and Prudential Securities sold 400 May and 300 July, traders said. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer and Merrill Lynch each bought 300 May.
In soyoil, Prudential Securities sold 600 lots May, Griffin Trading sold 500 May and Dean Witter sold 500 August, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 28,312 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 25,000 lots, against Monday's 31,910 lots.
